note: Doc 13 Part One, verbatim. Used when an object has no written response and no object-specific override. Pools ROTATE and never repeat consecutively. Doc 06: an unhandled combination gets a Thad line, never a generic refusal -- the pool is itself comedy.

PICK_UP: I gave it a good try. It stays where it is.
I'd better not. It's part of the town, and I'm hoping the town will like me.
USE: I've no plan for it yet. Give me time; I'm full of plans.
I'd need to want something from it first, and for once I don't.
That would want a purpose, and I'm saving mine for the big things.
OPEN: It doesn't open. Very little here does, but I live in hope.
There's no way into it. I checked, thoroughly and with optimism.
It isn't that kind of thing, more's the pity.
CLOSE: It's already as closed as it means to be.
It isn't open. I'd have noticed. I notice things.
There's nothing to close. I'm almost disappointed.
PUSH: It doesn't move. I've committed to this now, and it still doesn't move.
Nothing. And I put my back into it, too.
It stays. I'll give it this: it knows its own mind.
PULL: It stays where it is, and I look like a man pulling at a thing.
No. Not for want of trying.
It isn't coming. I can respect a thing that knows where it belongs.
TALK_TO: I've decided against it. I'll save my charm for something that can answer.
It's said nothing, I've said nothing, and we're both perfectly content.
I'd like it on record that I considered it.
GIVE: I'd have to be holding something first. It's the one rule of giving.

people.note: Doc 07: verbs other than TALK TO, pointed at a person. Thad's lines, not the character's, and shared across everyone -- 'I am not going to push a stranger' is the same sentiment whichever stranger it is. Before these existed, every verb on an ambient character opened their dialogue tree, so PUSH started a conversation.
LOOK_AT: A person! I've decided to be polite about it. I'm polite to everyone; it's half my charm.
PICK_UP: No. I've thought about it for exactly as long as it deserves.
PUSH: I've never pushed anybody in my life, and I'm not starting on a street this muddy.
PULL: Pulling a stranger is how a man ends up known for something.
OPEN: They're already as open as they mean to be.
CLOSE: One does not close a person. One is closed by them, usually at cards.
USE: I wouldn't know where to begin, and the beginning is the part people object to.
LISTEN_TO: Breathing, and the particular silence of somebody deciding whether I am worth their afternoon.
GIVE: Give what? I'm holding nothing, and I've grown rather attached to it.
